faqs.q: Why does Bire Noon look pinkish-purple when ground into powder?
faqs.a: Whole Bire Noon rock crystals look dark violet-black, but when finely ground into powder, authentic Bire Noon naturally turns a light pinkish-purple shade.

faqs.q: Why does Bire Noon have a distinctive savory smell?
faqs.a: Traditional kiln-curing creates natural iron sulfide and trace sulfur compounds, giving Bire Noon its signature savory aroma that pairs wonderfully with lemon, fruit, and dahi.

faqs.q: How is Bire Noon traditionally used in Nepali households?
faqs.a: In Nepali tradition, a pinch of Bire Noon in warm lemon water, ajwain (jwano) water, or buttermilk (mohi) is enjoyed after heavy meals.
